newsitem.title: USA: Berkshire Hathaway to acquire FlightSafety for $1.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: Berkshire Hathaway to acquire FlightSafety for $1.5 billion.

text.p: Berkshire Hathaway Inc., the holding company controlled by billionaire Warren Buffett, said Tuesday it was acquiring FlightSafety International Inc. for about $1.5 billion.

Berkshire Hathaway said it executed a definitive agreement in which FlightSafety, which provides high-technology training to operators of aircraft and ships, will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire.
The company said FlightSafety shareholders can elect to receive for each of their shares either $50 in cash or $48 in Berkshire common stock, for a total value of about $1.5 billion.
FlightSafety's stock soared after the news, adding $5.125 to $49 by midday on the New York Stock Exchange. Berkshire Hathaway's stock lost $100 to $31,800, also on the NYSE.

The number of shares of Berkshire to be received under the stock election will be based on the market price for Berkshire shares during a 5-day trading period ending the day before FlightSafety shareholders approve the merger.
The deal is subject to the approval of two-thirds of the outstanding shares of FlightSafety and certain other customary conditions.

Berkshire said shareholders owning more than 37 percent of FlightSafety's common stock -- mainly Chairman Albert L. Ueltschi and his family -- have stated that they intend to vote in favour of the transaction.

"I believe that this merger is in the best interests of FlightSafety, its customers, employees and shareholders. My family and I will vote our entire 37 percent holding in FlightSafety in favour of the merger," Ueltschi said in a statement.
"I look forward to continuing to run FlightSafety as part of Berkshire and working with Warren Buffett," Ueltschi added.
Ueltschi also said he will elect to receive Berkshire stock for all his FlightSafety shares.
"I personally consider Berkshire shares to be one of the finest investments that I could make and anticipate holding the shares indefinitely," he said.
Berkshire said the merger will qualify as a tax-free reorganization for FlightSafety shareholders electing to receive Berkshire common stock.
The board of directors of FlightSafety unanimously approved the merger agreement and recommended it to the shareholders for approval, the company said.
It is anticipated that the merger will close near the end of this year or early next year. FlightSafety is based at New York's LaGuardia Airport.
"FlightSafety is a business that I like, run by a man I like and admire," Berkshire Chairman Buffett said in a statement. "Al Ueltschi and FlightSafety will fit perfectly in the Berkshire family."
Berkshire Hathaway, based on Omaha, Neb., also has major stakes in The Coca-Cola Co., GEICO insurance company, American Express Co., Gillette Co. and The Disney Co.
